data.cultural_impact: The name Shifwat carries a significant cultural impact in Islam as it is known to be an all-encompassing name for anyone, not just limited to the Muslim community, who may bring comfort, relief, solace, or peace in various aspects of life. For instance, a person might be known as "Shifwat al-Masakh" (The Comforter), due to their healing touch in the medical field, or one might be named "Shifwat al-Hujur" (The Consoler), simply because they make others feel comforted and at ease in their presence. The term often serves as a reminder that, in a chaotic world, everyone holds the power to be a source of comfort and kindness to others, spreading positivity and harmony in their wake.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, the name Shifwat holds deep spiritual significance, as it is mentioned in the Quran as a name for Allah, the Almighty. Surah Ar-Rahman, verse 64 reads, "And indeed, We have granted religious sanctity to the house [Makkah] which We have mentioned [in the Quran]. And take, [O Muhammad], from its [mihrab] a green [branch] neither of it nor of those around it being wet. And mention the name of Allah upon it; and [from off it] pray [Rakah]. And We have appointed it for those who make Tawaf (pilgrimage around it) as compassion and pleasure." In this verse, Allah is identified as Shifwat universally, and, thus, the one who grants comfort and tranquility to the believers and the afflicted souls. This is a constant reminder of the immense power and ever-loving nature of Allah, who, in His infinite mercy, bestows comfort upon His creation, whether through the blessings of His divine wisdom or through the love and kindness of other human beings.

historical_references.reference: Shifwat al-Mamun was a governor of Egypt during the Abbasid Caliphate in the late 9th century. He is known for his patronage of scholars and the construction of several notable structures such as the Shifwat Mosque in Fustat.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliphate, Egypt, Patronage of scholars, Construction of Shifwat Mosque

historical_references.reference: Shaykh Shifwat Shah Hamadani was a Sufi saint and scholar from the 13th century. He is revered in both India and Pakistan for his spiritual teachings and is the founder of the Hamadaniya order.
historical_references.context: Sufi saint and scholar, Founder of Hamadaniya order, India and Pakistan
